 Louisiana election results: Letlow, Johnson, Higgins, Carter, other races decided 
 Julia Letlow wins Louisiana’s U.S. Senate race, Hillar Moore secures reelection as district attorney, and Chauna Banks and Blake Miguez advance to a congressional runoff. 
 By Gray Louisiana Published : Nov. 3, 2026 at 6:00 AM CST | Updated : Nov. 3, 2026 at 11:42 PM CST Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google BATON ROUGE, La. (WAFB) - Several major Louisiana election races have been called Tuesday night, Nov. 3, with Republican Julia Letlow winning the U.S. Senate race.
 U.S. House Speaker Mike Johnson and U.S. Rep. Troy Carter won reelection to Congress.
 CLICK HERE FOR LIVE ELECTION RESULTS 
 FULL ELECTION RESULTS FROM SECRETARY OF STATE 
 Julia Letlow to win Louisiana U.S. Senate race
 Republican U.S. Rep. Julia Letlow defeated Democrat Jamie Davis in the race to replace U.S. Sen. Bill Cassidy.
 Letlow, who currently represents Louisiana’s 5th Congressional District, won the Republican nomination earlier this year after defeating state Treasurer John Fleming in a June runoff.
 Davis, a farmer from Tensas Parish, secured the Democratic nomination after defeating New Orleans businessman Gary Crockett.
 Davis delivered a message directed at Louisiana Gov. Jeff Landry.
 “Jeff Landry, you’re on notice,” Davis said.
 Letlow becomes the first Republican woman elected to the U.S. Senate from Louisiana.
 She will serve a six-year term alongside Republican Sen. John Kennedy.
 Jamie Davis, Julia Letlow ((Louisiana Illuminator photos)) Hillar Moore to win East Baton Rouge district attorney race
 Incumbent District Attorney Hillar Moore III has won reelection, defeating challenger Ryan Thompson in Tuesday’s election.
 Moore, who was first elected in 2008, is expected to secure another term overseeing criminal prosecutions in East Baton Rouge Parish’s 19th Judicial District.
 The election marked Moore’s first contested reelection campaign since taking office. Thompson, a former assistant public defender, challenged Moore’s approach to criminal justice and public safety.
 Incumbent East Baton Rouge District Attorney Hillar Moore III (right) faces challenger Ryan Thompson (left) in the Nov. 3, 2026, election. (WAFB) Brad Cascio projected to win Livingston Parish district attorney race
 Assistant District Attorney Brad Cascio will become the next district attorney for Louisiana’s 21st Judicial District, defeating former state Rep. Sherman Mack.
 The two Republicans were competing to replace longtime District Attorney Scott Perrilloux, who is retiring after 30 years in office.
 Cascio has emphasized his years of experience prosecuting criminal cases in the district attorney’s office.
 The 21st Judicial District includes Livingston, Tangipahoa and St. Helena parishes.
 Troy Carter, Clay Higgins and Mike Johnson projected to win reelection
 Three incumbent members of Louisiana’s congressional delegation to win another term in Washington.
 Democratic U.S. Rep. Troy Carter won reelection in Louisiana’s 2nd Congressional District, which includes portions of Baton Rouge and New Orleans.
 Republican U.S. Rep. Clay Higgins won another term representing the 3rd Congressional District, which includes much of southwest Louisiana and Acadiana.
 U.S. House Speaker Mike Johnson, a Republican, won reelection in Louisiana’s 4th Congressional District.
 Johnson’s reelection to Congress does not automatically guarantee he will remain House speaker. Members of the new Congress will select their leadership when the House convenes in January.
 Chauna Banks, Blake Miguez headed to runoff in 6th Congressional District
 Democrat Chauna Banks and Republican state Sen. Blake Miguez are headed to a Dec. 12 runoff in Louisiana’s redrawn 6th Congressional District.
 The two advanced from a field of 10 candidates after no one received more than 50% of the vote Tuesday, Nov. 3.
 Banks is a former East Baton Rouge Metro Council member, while Miguez is a state senator from New Iberia.
 The candidates are competing for the seat being vacated by Democratic U.S. Rep. Cleo Fields, who did not seek reelection after the district was redrawn earlier this year.
 The runoff will determine who represents the district in Congress beginning in January 2027.
 School board and judicial races
 Voters also decided several East Baton Rouge Parish School Board and judicial elections.
